note: Every rate here was read on 2026-10-14 from the source named in the row's sourceUrl. Rows marked sourceQuality 'vendor' came from the provider's own page or public pricing API: AWS from the EC2 on-demand price list that backs aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand (JSON at b0.p.awsstatic.com/pricing/2.0/meteredUnitMaps/ec2, publication date 2026-10-12) with spot from AWS's own Spot price feed; Azure from the unauthenticated Azure Retail Prices API (prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices), where reserved is the published 1-year reservation total divided by 8760 hours; Oracle from Oracle's public price list API (apexapps.oracle.com/pls/apex/cetools, lastUpdated 2026-10-08), whose metric is per GPU per hour and is multiplied by the GPU count Oracle lists for that shape; CoreWeave, Lambda, RunPod, Together, Nebius and Crusoe from their public pricing pages, with per-GPU rates multiplied by the GPU count the same page states for the instance. GCP is the one exception and is marked 'aggregator': Google renders its GPU pricing tables client-side and its Cloud Billing Catalog API needs a key, so no GCP rate could be read from a Google page in this pass. Reference region per provider: AWS us-east-1; GCP us-central1; Azure eastus, except ND H200 v5 and ND MI300X v5 which Azure does not offer in eastus and are priced in eastus2 (the same rate as westus3); Oracle us-ashburn-1, which is Oracle's uniform commercial list price. CoreWeave is priced from its US region tab. Lambda, RunPod, Together, Nebius and Crusoe publish a single rate per plan with no per-region table, which is recorded as such in each row's region. reservedPerHr and spotPerHr are populated only where the provider publishes a concrete rate. They are null, with the reason in the row's note, wherever the provider instead advertises a percentage ('up to 60% off' at CoreWeave, 'up to 35% less' at Nebius), a dynamic floor ('from $0.79/GPU-hour' at Nebius), 'Contact sales' (Crusoe, Together B300 reserved), or a spot meter priced identically to on-demand (Azure ND H200 v5, ND GB200 v6) — a number derived from a discount percentage is not a quote and is not recorded as one. AWS publishes no flat reserved rate for the P-family on a public page; Capacity Blocks and Savings Plans are separate products. AWS spot rates are live market prices that move continuously, so treat them as indicative. AMD MI325X is absent: no per-hour rate for it was found at any of the ten providers surveyed. This file is hand-refreshed and goes stale quickly — GPU pricing moved 17-21% at some providers in 2026 alone. See #54 for a scraper proposal.
